rv.q: A journalist himself, Mr. Zax shows a greater flair here for storytelling structure than he does for dialogue.
But “Aftermath,” opening tonight at A.R.T./NY, is too flawed a play for the issues to hit home anywhere near as effectively.
Sadly, by the time it reaches its conclusion, the quartet of actors are spent and so is the audience—and not in a good way.

cn.t: David Zax's family drama about a journalist's Taliban kidnapping strains under its ambitions, with critics finding the play too flawed to effectively land its moral themes despite tackling weighty issues of privilege and virtue.
